question:
A 79-year-old man who currently smokes presents for follow-up of an asymptomatic ascending thoracic
aortic aneurysm. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a BMI of 31. He is on a
beta-blocker and a statin. His blood pressure is 129/77 mm Hg, heart rate is 60 beats per minute, and
LDL cholesterol level is 68 mg/dL (reference range, <130). A recent chest CT shows an increase in the
aneurysm’s diameter from 4.8 cm one year ago to 5.0 cm currently. Echocardiography reveals
moderate calcific aortic stenosis with an aortic valve area of 1.2 cm² and a mean gradient of 27 mm Hg.
The patient denies symptoms such as angina, syncope, near-syncope, or congestive heart failure.
Which of the following interventions is the most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Initiate anticoagulation therapy (B) Initiate calcium channel blocker (C) Schedule cardiac
catheterization (D) Increase beta-blocker dosage (E) Smoking cessation (F) Add ACE inhibitor therapy
(G) Increase statin dosage (H) Schedule urgent endovascular repair (I) Aortic aneurysm repair alone
(J) Aortic valve replacement and aortic aneurysm repair
 A. Schedule urgent endovascular repair
B. Aortic valve replacement and aortic aneurysm repair
C. Aortic aneurysm repair alone
D. Add ACE inhibitor therapy
E. Smoking cessation
F. Increase beta-blocker dosage
G. Schedule cardiac catheterization
H. Increase statin dosage
I. Initiate anticoagulation therapy
J. Initiate calcium channel blocker
